clue.text: Go with Bill and his guests

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be settled
a host's guests are his company

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to join a host at a party along with all the other guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to travel alongside them as a companion.

clue.text: A cold half-moon is over the port

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: is over, in a down clue, sends the curved shape back upward

parts.note: a half-moon is a curved shape, an arc

explanation.surface: A chilly crescent moon hangs above the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is over' turns ARC into CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana, a seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Cheer up! Trapped by a rebel? It's only a pretence

indicators.note: trapped by means the reversed cheer is enclosed by the rebel's name

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, sends the cheer reading upward

parts.note: rah is a cheer

explanation.surface: Someone told to cheer up after being caught by an insurgent dismisses it as an act.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450; in a down clue 'up' turns the cheer upward. 'It's only' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence or sham.

clue.text: Physicist, in one way, is a plant operator

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist
I is the Roman numeral one
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A scientist turns out to work in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines in a factory or plant.

clue.text: Card players in a tournament initially cutting

parts.note: bridge men are players of the card game bridge

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of tournament

explanation.surface: Card players taking part in a tournament cut the pack at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is a noun here: a shortening of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridgement is a shortened version of a text.

clue.text: Cry of defiance raised in dance

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the dance's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance

explanation.surface: Someone shouts defiance while dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah is an exclamation of scorn or derision.

clue.text: .Volunteers express disapproval of prohibition

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Volunteers voice their objection to a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social or religious ban on something.

clue.text: "Imitate the action of the" (Hen.V)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Henry V's speech before Harfleur, wanting the animal named

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry V the king urges: 'Then imitate the action of the tiger'.
explanation.definitionFit: The line from the play names a big striped cat as the creature to copy.

clue.text: Composer in libel controversy

indicators.note: controversy stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician caught up in a defamation dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controversy' rearranges IN and LIBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera composer, of Norma.

clue.text: Soldiers hop around in religious rite

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: around means the word for hop goes round the word in

parts.note: a hop is a dance

explanation.surface: Troops jump about during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative rite or sacrament, such as communion.

clue.text: Tea — cure perhaps for writer

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word cure may be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A cup of tea as a possible remedy for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea' looks like part of the anagram, but only the word cure is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Chaucer was the medieval English poet of The Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Cheated about a horse the French bargained for?

indicators.note: about means the word for cheated goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to have someone is to cheat or fool them, so had means cheated
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, shortened to GG
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone was swindled over a horse they had negotiated to buy from the French.
explanation.walkthrough: GG (gee-gee) is nursery talk for a horse; the question mark and 'for' dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to bargain persistently over a price.

clue.text: Take part in a dramatic fiddle

indicators.note: take part in tells us to take a part of the next word, its interior letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to play a role in a theatrical swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside drAMATIc.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin made by the famous Cremona family of luthiers.

clue.text: Another way for a girl to get a translation'

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, as for Diana
a version is a rendering of a text into another language

explanation.surface: A girl takes an alternative route to obtain a translated text.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is an alternative route laid on when a road is closed.

clue.text: Evita, raging, is changing colour…

definitions.note: verb, colouring in streaks; the answer is its -ing form

indicators.note: is changing means the letters of these two words are altered in order

explanation.surface: Evita flies into a rage and her face changes colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is changing' rearranges EVITA and RAGING.
explanation.definitionFit: To variegate is to mark with patches of different hues.

clue.text: A digit to point

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A finger used to point something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digit' suggests a finger, but the foot has digits too.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are the digits on the foot.

clue.text: Keen ditch worker

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic labourer who digs ditches.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and sharp, as a keen edge.

clue.text: Drunkenness gets into brain that is confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of these words are muddled into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Alcohol gets to the brain and leaves it muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges INTO, BRAIN and IE; 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriation is the state of being intoxicated by alcohol.

clue.text: Heed a military command

explanation.surface: An order to soldiers to pay notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Heed is notice taken; Attention! is the drill order to stand straight.

clue.text: Name given to people in medical specialism as a right

indicators.note: in places the name and the people inside the medical specialism

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital specialism
a title is a name, as of a book
men means people, as in men and women of a crew

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a title for staff in a hospital department is theirs by right.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat; 'given to' joins the name and the people, and 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entitlement is something one has a lawful claim to.

clue.text: He showed the fantastic uses of heroism

definitions.text: He showed the fantastic uses of heroism

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hero who demonstrated the wonderful applications of bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges THE and USES; the whole clue also describes the hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the Greek hero who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Welcome a girl on her return

indicators.note: on her return means the girl's name is read back to front

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is greeted as she comes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is a Latin greeting, hail.

clue.text: Finish a letter to a girl

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Completing a letter written to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to accomplish or bring to completion.

clue.text: Royal needlewoman

parts.note: seems to describe a queen who sews, but points to a monarch whose name is attached to a famous London obelisk, the Needle

explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle is an ancient Egyptian obelisk on the Thames Embankment in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen gives her name to the obelisk called her Needle.

clue.text: Office messenger unknown in the plant

parts.note: in India a peon is an office errand-runner
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An office errand-runner is lost among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A peony is a garden flower with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Said to be a knack? By no 'means

indicators.note: said to be signals that the answer sounds like the phrase for a knack

parts.note: know-how is practical skill, a knack

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a skill is reputed to be what is needed, and is firmly told no.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect word meaning in no way at all.

clue.text: Western crawlers — an influential group in American society

definitions.text: an influential group in American society
definitions.note: the answer is plural, members of the group

parts.note: asps are snakes, which crawl

explanation.surface: Creepy-crawlies of the Wild West compared to America's elite.
explanation.walkthrough: WASPs are White Anglo-Saxon Protestants, the traditional US establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: White Anglo-Saxon Protestants have historically formed the US social elite.

clue.text: Excellent service, sound enough to make one solvent

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A tennis player's serve is good enough to clear all their debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' looks financial, but it is a liquid that dissolves; 'enough to make one' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a volatile liquid used to dissolve paint and nail varnish.

clue.text: You' sound sheepish

indicators.note: sound tells us the word you is to be heard, not read

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Someone is told they seem embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' is read as relating to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is the word, so it is sheepish in a literal sense.

clue.text: Coldness of manner since one's blunder?

indicators.note: a blunder is a botch, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is I, and one's gives I with S, IS

explanation.surface: Someone has been frosty ever since making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunder' rearranges SINCE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is frostiness, a chilly unfriendly bearing.

clue.text: Bad-tempered youth leader on '. trial

indicators.note: on means the leader comes after the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A youth club leader who is irritable while on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable and short-tempered.

clue.text: Branch of the army in manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Part of the army is out on exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Engineers are an army corps; to engineer is also to contrive or manipulate cleverly.
